agree.reason: The page is clear and believable, but a four-chair owner who pays her cousin $600 a year will see $199 a month and has no reason to give up a cheaper arrangement she likes, so she probably won't book the call.

honest.reason: No numbers are invented and the missed deadlines are admitted, but the heading 'Clean books cost less at tax time' turns what 9 of 31 clients reported into a general rule.

works_the_facts.reason: Every figure is repeated raw and none is worked out: retention could be stated as 29 of 31 with no one leaving over the service, and the yearly price ($2,388) could be set against the $600 and the possible $800 tax saving.

right_comparison.reason: The only alternative described is the owner doing her books at 11pm, while this reader's actual alternative is a once-a-year relative who costs far less, and the page never deals with that.

qualification.reason: The 10th-of-the-month deadline and the 3 misses give the reader a date and a number she can check, but the page doesn't say what happens to her if a close is late.

objections.reason: The objections this reader will have (the price compared with her cousin, loyalty to him, and whether a four-chair salon needs a monthly service) go unanswered, while the page spends space on being a solo operator, which she hadn't questioned.

fit.reason: It is about 330 words of sales-page copy with clear sections and ends with a button to book the call, as the brief asked.
